<reflection>
The first experiment provided baseline kinetic data. The fitting results show that most mechanisms (M1 through M19) have very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, all within a narrow range (approximately -23.8 to -22.5), indicating that they fit the data almost equally well given the single experimental condition. M20 has a significantly higher NLL (-12.6), making it much less plausible. The small differences among the other mechanisms mean that the first experiment alone cannot reliably distinguish between them. The aim of the first turn was to establish a baseline, which was achieved. Now, we need a second experiment that will provide additional information to reduce uncertainty across the entire set of plausible mechanisms.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
We propose to increase the catalyst concentration while keeping the substrate concentration constant and no initial product. This design probes the dependence of the reaction rate on catalyst concentration, which varies among mechanisms. For example:
- Simple Michaelis-Menten (M1) predicts initial rate proportional to catalyst concentration (linear scaling).
- Dimerization mechanisms (M2, M3) may show quadratic scaling at low catalyst if the dimer is the active form.
- Inactivation mechanisms (M9, M11-M19) could lead to sublinear scaling if inactivation consumes catalyst.
- Mechanisms with catalyst activation (M6, M8) might exhibit more complex dependence.
By holding substrate constant at 1.0 M (a moderate value that avoids saturation in the first experiment), we isolate the catalyst effect. A catalyst concentration of 0.05 M (5× higher than the first experiment) is chosen to be in a regime where nonlinear effects may become apparent without driving the system to extreme saturation (catalyst is still substoichiometric relative to substrate). This condition should yield kinetic profiles that help discriminate multiple mechanisms simultaneously, as it tests a fundamental property—the reaction order in catalyst—that differs across many candidates.
</hypothesis>
